what: First Solar makes solar panels using cadmium telluride thin film rather than the silicon used by almost everyone else. It is the largest solar manufacturer headquartered in the United States and sells mostly to utility-scale projects.
customers: Utility-scale solar developers and independent power producers, mainly in the United States and India.
money: thin-film solar modules sold under multi-year contracts
moat: A manufacturing technology no Chinese competitor uses, which keeps it outside the silicon price war and qualifies its panels for US content-based tax credits.
risks: US clean energy tax policy determines much of the economics and has been changed before
Utility-scale project timing can shift, delaying deliveries
Silicon panel prices have collapsed, which pressures pricing even where it does not compete directly
opportunities: Revenue grew about 24% last year and about 26% a year over three years
Operating margin of 31% with cash of $1.6 billion and almost no debt
Analysts see large upside, with a contracted backlog stretching years out
watch: The contracted backlog, average selling price per watt, and US policy on tax credits.
